clue.text: Given advance notice of wanderer going astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was warned in advance about a traveller who has lost the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going astray' asks for the ten letters of OF and WANDERER to be rearranged; 'wanderer' alone is two letters short.
explanation.definitionFit: To be warned beforehand is to be given notice of something before it happens.

clue.text: Forget to leave out

explanation.surface: Neglecting to depart on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean failing to include something, either through forgetfulness or on purpose.

clue.text: He's in charge but has a leader

definitions.text: He's in charge but has a leader

parts.words: He's in charge but has a leader
parts.note: a paradox: someone at the top who still has a leader, read as the newspaper boss whose paper carries a leading article

explanation.walkthrough: A 'leader' in British newspapers is the editorial column, which the person running the paper oversees.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper is in charge and is responsible for its leading article.

clue.text: An hotel looks different in Ireland

indicators.note: if something looks different its appearance is changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel in Ireland has had a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks different' rearranges the seven letters of AN HOTEL. ATHLONE is a town in the centre of Ireland, on the River Shannon.
explanation.definitionFit: Athlone is a town in the Irish midlands, so it is a place found in Ireland.

clue.text: Girl has lost a pattern

indicators.note: losing something means it goes, so the named letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman has mislaid a dress pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' takes A away from NORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or typical model to follow.

clue.text: Being abandoned, many felt irritated

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a crossword stand-in for many
itched means felt an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: Left behind, a crowd grew annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' as D (500 in Roman numerals) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditched is an informal word for dumped or discarded.

clue.text: Shrewd fielder in sticky leg trap

parts.note: fly is British slang for shrewd or knowing
a catcher is a fielder who takes the ball, as in baseball or cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket close fielder lurks in the leg trap waiting for a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a 'leg trap' is a ring of close catchers on the leg side; here it is a sticky trap for insects with legs. FLY as shrewd is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Flypaper is a sticky strip that traps insects, the creatures with legs that it snares.

clue.text: Chap under terrible strain becomes acerbic

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under means coming after in the answer
terrible suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of strain are scrambled

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A man put under great pressure turns sharp-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges STRAIN to ASTRIN, and 'under' puts GENT below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are sharp and biting, just as acerbic ones are.

clue.text: They're given to those who beg for weapons, we hear

definitions.text: They're given to those who beg

indicators.note: we hear signals a word said out loud that is written differently

parts.note: arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Beggars ask for guns, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent ARMS and ALMS sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable gifts of money or food are handed to beggars.

clue.text: Madrid is in her itinerary, but part can be cut off

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, signalling letters buried inside them

explanation.surface: A trip plan that includes Madrid may be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of Madrid through to the start of itinerary. To cut off an heir is to disinherit.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone off, as in a will, is to deprive them of their inheritance.

clue.text: Agree to old lag's dog

parts.note: an old lag is British slang for a convict, a con
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Agreeing to take on a former prisoner's dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old lag' is British slang for a long-serving prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to be of the same opinion.

clue.text: A highly vocal female

parts.note: reads as a loud woman but means a singer of the top vocal range

explanation.definitionFit: A singer with the highest voice range, usually a woman.

clue.text: Security zone for motorist

parts.note: safety is security from harm
a belt is a zone, as in a green belt

explanation.surface: A protected area set aside for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A seatbelt restrains a driver in a car crash.

clue.text: Assembly, part male in composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gathering that is partly male in make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges the ten letters PARTMALEIN; 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is a legislative gathering of elected members.

clue.text: A spot of refreshment

parts.note: reads as a small drink but means a place in the desert where travellers find water

explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert with water offers relief to travellers.

clue.text: Hear only half the score, yet cheer

parts.note: taken as written
a score is twenty, so half of it is ten

explanation.surface: Listening to just part of the music is still uplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' means twenty here, not a musical score or match result.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage or lift their spirits.

clue.text: Field division that takes years to train

definitions.text: Field division that takes years to train

parts.words: Field division that takes years to train
parts.note: reads like an army unit needing long drilling, but means a boundary of shrubs that slowly grows and is trimmed into shape

explanation.definitionFit: A row of bushes separating fields, slowly grown and shaped over time.

clue.text: Facilitated return by stamped addressed envelope to editor

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: SAE is the British abbreviation for stamped addressed envelope

explanation.surface: A writer made things simple by enclosing a stamped addressed envelope for the editor's reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns SAE into EAS. An SAE is sent so the reply is posted back free.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means made easier or helped along.

clue.text: Food and money for the journey

explanation.surface: Snacks and cash needed for a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is food served at a meal, and also the price paid to travel.

clue.text: Footwear she has a hole in

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
O is round like a hole

explanation.surface: A woman's footwear has worn through.
explanation.walkthrough: O inside SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is something worn on the foot.

clue.text: Give hot tips at barbers

parts.note: sounds like passing on racing tips at the hairdresser, but means scorching the ends of hair, an old barber's treatment

explanation.definitionFit: Barbers once lightly burned hair ends with a flame.

clue.text: Deformed, so tried a body-building drug

indicators.note: deformed means put out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Misshapen from trying a muscle-building substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deformed' rearranges SO TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are taken to build muscle.

clue.text: Question cut-back by colliery

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Grilling a pit about its cutbacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the synonym for cut round; the hyphen in 'cut-back' disguises the reversal signal as an everyday word for a reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine someone is to interrogate them closely.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen, a T S Eliot production

indicators.note: a production is something made, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Addressing the audience at a staging of the poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' rearranges the letters of T S ELIOT. 'Ladies' and 'Gents' are British signs for public lavatories.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs reading Ladies and Gentlemen mark public lavatories.

clue.text: Passage taken from book unless it holds reader at the start

indicators.note: holds means one piece contains the other

parts.note: except means unless

indicators.note: the start of the word gives just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A book extract, unless the reader is holding it at the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the first letter of 'reader', goes inside EXCEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract from a longer text.

clue.text: Point to eleven the French made outcasts

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, and a team of eleven players in cricket
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Pointing at a team of the French who became pariahs.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football team is often called an XI.
explanation.definitionFit: Exiles are people banished from their homeland.

clue.text: S African doctor brought in by military aircraft

indicators.note: being brought in by something means going inside it

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A South African medic flown in by an air force plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'military aircraft' looks like part of the wordplay but is the definition; 'brought in by' puts the medical degree inside the settler.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber is a warplane built to drop bombs.

clue.text: Refrain from piling up dishes

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: pots are cooking dishes

explanation.surface: Advice to stop stacking the crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piling up' reverses POTS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from something is to cease or hold back.

clue.text: The lady's ring is one much admired

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Her ring belongs to a man she idolises.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a person idolised for courage or achievement.

clue.text: One who is deep in the letters of Freud and Eliot

indicators.note: the letters of the two names are taken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker absorbed in the correspondence of a psychoanalyst and a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deep' is a cricket term for fielding positions near the boundary, far from the batsman, not profound thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer stationed far out near the boundary fields in the deep.

clue.text: Family row

explanation.surface: A domestic quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A line is a lineage of descent, and also a row of things in a straight series.

clue.text: Slump causing gloom

explanation.surface: An economic downturn leading to low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A depression is an economic downturn, and also a state of deep sadness.
